name: Anthony Chabot Campground
reservation_method: Park office (not reservations): (510) 690-6676, or 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4502
nightly_entry_cutoff: 10:00 PM, and it is a lock-out rather than a courtesy: entry gates are locked every night at 10pm and NO entry is possible until they re-open at 8am the next morning. Campers may EXIT at any time, so a late departure is fine and a late arrival is not. Stated by EBRPD, unlike Del Valle's cutoff, which this project holds only as a visitor's near-miss report.
fee_notes: Drive-in camping $35/night; hike-in camping $25/night; RV hook-up camping $45/night. Limited overflow parking $8/night/vehicle. RV sewage disposal $20/use ($20 per use for non-campers). Firewood $10/bundle and charcoal $15/bag are sold at the campground kiosk. Park accepts cash, Visa, MasterCard and Discover. Fees subject to change.
notes: SITE COMPOSITION CONFIRMED by EBRPD's own page, having been carried as unconfirmed web-search figures earlier: 53 drive-to tent sites, 10 walk-to tent sites and 12 RV/trailer sites with full hookups (sewer, water, 30-amp electrical), 75 in total. The earlier figure also claimed 1 developed group site inside that 75; it is not -- 53+10+12 accounts for all 75, and Anthony Chabot's seven group camps are separate bookings. MAXIMUM RV LENGTH IS 35 FEET on hookup sites. Every site has a picnic table and a fire ring with grill; restrooms include hot showers; firewood and charcoal are sold at the campground kiosk. Open year-round, in a eucalyptus grove overlooking Lake Chabot, with fishing at Lake Chabot nearby and registered campers parking free at the Lake Chabot Marina. No day-use parking in the campground. The 10 walk-to sites are why access_mode is not uniform here and are priced separately at the hike-in rate; the row is tagged drive_in for the other 65. Stay limit is 15 consecutive days and 30 total a year with a 2-day break, which matches Ordinance 38 s.400.3(b) rather than adding to it. DRIVE TIME IS STATED TWICE AND DIFFERENTLY ON THE SAME EBRPD PAGE -- 20 minutes from downtown Oakland in the park overview, 35 minutes from downtown Oakland and the airport in the campground section. Both are recorded because the page contradicts itself; neither is approximate in a way this project can resolve, and drive time gates nothing, so no conflict thread was opened for it.

name: Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay
park: Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay
notes: Open year-round. Reported composition, unconfirmed: about 60 paved sites with water, sewer and 50 amp electrical hookups, taking tent, walk-in, bike and RV camping. THE PARK FIELD IS UNCONFIRMED and is set to this campground's own name because EBRPD lists it as a park in its own right, while the same listing describes it as located within Coyote Hills Regional Park -- which appears separately in that list with its own camping. Which unit governs entrance fees and gate hours here is exactly the kind of question this field is joined on, so it is flagged rather than decided. As with Anthony Chabot, every fact here is from web-search summaries rather than a page read firsthand.

name: Bort Meadow Group Camp
nightly_entry_cutoff: 10:00 PM -- the park page gives campground and group camp gate hours as 8am-10pm.
notes: One of seven group camps at Anthony Chabot, and the only one EBRPD names on the pages read here; the other six are unnamed and no rows were invented for them. The seven range in capacity from 35 to 300 campers and all include picnic tables, BBQ, fire ring, water and chemical or vault toilets. A MINIMUM OF 10 PEOPLE is required to use a group campsite, so these are not an option for a small party -- EBRPD directs groups of 17 or more away from the family campground and toward these. EQUESTRIAN CAMPING is available here by reservation, the only EBRPD equestrian camping this project holds outside Del Valle. This camp's own capacity, fee and site count are UNCONFIRMED -- the 35-to-300 range covers all seven together and cannot be read as this one's. Bort Meadow is also a staging area off Redwood Road.
